diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consider the Lyapunov equation~\eqref{alg:statIterGLE:lyap} with $\fA$ Hurwitz

issues.failure_explanation: For L = I⊗A + A⊗I with merely Hurwitz A, sigma_min(L) = 2 sigma_min(A) is false. Counterexample: A = [[-1,-10],[10,-1]] is Hurwitz and normal, with sigma_min(A)=sqrt(101); the eigenvalues of L are -2±20i and -2 (double), so sigma_min(L)=2 while 2 sigma_min(A)≈20.1. A symmetric residual R aligned with the eigendirection of L for the eigenvalue -2 gives ||E||_F = (1/2)||R||_F, violating the claimed ||E||_2 ≤ ||R||_F/(2 sigma_min(A)) by a factor ≈10 (unbounded in general, e.g. whenever lambda_i(A)+lambda_j(A) is small relative to |lambda_i(A)|). The correct constant is sigma_min(L). The same false identity is used as an equality in (33) (hence also in the rescaling (34) and the claim gamma<1), and the proof of teo1 additionally applies prop1's spectral-norm bound to Frobenius norms, so teo1's bound (50) inherits the defect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 2 sigma_min(A) by sigma_min(L) (or a rigorous, computable lower bound obtained e.g. by inverse iteration on the Lyapunov operator) throughout prop1, teo1, (33)-(34) and the stopping-criterion constants; all certification guarantees then survive with the corrected constant.
issues.overall_effect: prop1's residual bound (12), teo1's certified bound (50), the computable bound (33), the rescaling (34) with the claim gamma<1, and the stopping criteria promising ||X - X~||_2 ≤ tol (abstract, introduction, Section 3, conclusions) are unfounded: the certified tolerance can be violated by an unbounded factor whenever sigma_min(L) << 2 sigma_min(A), so the advertised rigorous error guarantees for the GLE solver are not established.
issues.title: False identity sigma_min(L)=2 sigma_min(A) invalidates the Lyapunov residual bound and the GLE error certification
issues.why_classification: A local change of the constant (and of how it is computed) repairs prop1 and teo1 with the certification guarantee intact; no proof architecture or substantive result is abandoned, although the corrected constant can be much smaller and costlier to evaluate.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds mu*w^T A_j^T w <= -mu*sigma_min(A_j)||w||^2, citing only dissipativity (w^T A_j w < 0). Dissipativity gives w^T A_j w <= lambda_max((A_j+A_j^T)/2)||w||^2, which can be much less negative than -sigma_min(A_j)||w||^2: for A = [[-eps,K],[-K,-eps]] (dissipative for eps>0, even normal), lambda_max(sym A) = -eps while sigma_min(A) = sqrt(K^2+eps^2) >> eps. The inference is therefore invalid, the sufficient condition (22) with kappa(A_j)=sigma_1/sigma_n is too weak (the argument actually requires mu >= sigma_1(A_j)/|lambda_max(sym A_j)| * ||X - X~||_2, unboundedly larger for nearly skew-symmetric dissipative matrices), and X^ = X~ + mu*I can fail to satisfy the LMI (9a) under the stated hypotheses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace kappa(A_j) in (22) (and correspondingly in (eqn:cond:LMI)) by sigma_1(A_j)/|lambda_max((A_j+A_j^T)/2)|, the ratio actually implied by dissipativity, and adjust the subsequent discussion of the perturbation magnitude; teo4 and its uses then hold with the corrected constant.
issues.overall_effect: teo4's guarantee that the perturbed Gramian X^ = X~ + mu*I satisfies the reachability LMI (9a) is unproven and false in general under hypothesis (22); the recommended choice mu^ = tol*max_j kappa(A_j) (eqn:cond:LMI) and the LMI-enforcement strategy numerically exercised in Section 5.1 inherit the insufficient perturbation size.
issues.title: teo4: dissipativity does not imply w^T A_j w <= -sigma_min(A_j)||w||^2; the stated perturbation size is insufficient
issues.why_classification: A local change of the constant in hypothesis (22) repairs the theorem and all its uses; the required perturbation can become much larger for lightly damped, strongly non-normal modes (a quantitative weakening only), while the result and method remain comparable.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows directly by applying the sub-additivity of the square root function to \Cref{teo5} and standard balance truncation error arguments; see, for instance, \cite[Sec.~7]{PetWL13}.
the dominant contribution to the error bound at higher values of $\stateDimRed$ stems from the violation of the \LMI conditions, i.e., the component $\iota(\stateDimRed, \switchedSysRedJumps)$

issues.failure_explanation: In teo5 the quantities G_{c,o} enter the bound as -G_{c,o} under the square root, so subadditive extraction yields +max(-G_{c,o},0)^{1/2}. teo6 instead subtracts G_{c,o}^{1/2}H(-G_{c,o}): when G_{c,o}<0 the square root is not real-valued (the formula is ill-defined), and under the natural repair the term is subtracted, making the right-hand side smaller than the provable bound, so the stated inequality can fail (an error bound that underestimates). Moreover, G_{c,o,q}(s_{k+1},s_k) and H_{c,o,q}(s_{k+1},s_k) are never defined - teo5 defines G,H only for the full FOM/ROM pair (n, n - m~) - the index s_k is defined with a reused summation index and an undefined 'n tilde', the sum range requires the undefined s_{n~+1}, and the two-line proof does not establish the iterative decomposition. The paper's own numerical definition of iota (eqn:iota), presented as a positive dominant component of the estimate, contradicts the stated minus sign.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the G term of (eq:err:est:3) and (eqn:iota) as + sum_k (-G_{c,o,q}(s_{k+1},s_k))^{1/2} H(-G_{c,o,q}(s_{k+1},s_k)), define s_k and the intermediate-size quantities G,H (principal blocks of the balanced M_c, M_o together with the trajectories of the intermediate reduced systems), and spell out the iterative application of teo5 (legitimate since Sigma_j is diagonal).
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central new a-posteriori error bound (eq:err:est:3) for the PBR method is not a valid, well-defined bound as stated; the error-estimate decomposition tau, chi, iota, varphi (eqn:tau:tilde - eqn:err:est:fin) and the Black-Scholes error-bound evaluation in Section 5.2 inherit the defective formula.
issues.title: teo6: the PBR error bound is invalid as stated (sign-inverted/ill-defined G term, undefined intermediate quantities and indices)
issues.why_classification: The mathematical content of the bound is recoverable by a contained correction (sign fix plus precise definitions and completion of the standard iterative argument); no guarantee or regime is lost, but the repair is more than a routine typo fix because the statement's quantities must be properly defined and the derivation completed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: if $\fA_j$ is normal, i.e., $\fA_j\fA^{*}_j=\fA_j^{*}\fA_j$, then~\eqref{eqn:ass:ndeAj} holds

issues.failure_explanation: For the defined matrices (n = 200 >= 2), A_1 = -I + (1/2)L and A_2 = -2I + (4/5)L - (1/5)L^T (L the down-shift) satisfy A_1 A_1^T - A_1^T A_1 = (1/4)(LL^T - L^TL) = (1/4)diag(1,0,...,0,-1) != 0 and A_2 A_2^T - A_2^T A_2 = (15/25)(LL^T - L^TL) != 0, so neither is normal by the paper's own definition. Normality was invoked as the route to the dissipativity hypothesis (21) of teo4; that hypothesis does hold for these matrices by direct computation (A_j + A_j^T is strictly diagonally dominant with negative diagonal), so only the stated justification is false.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, both $\fA_1$ and $\fA_2$ are normal matrices, so the hypothesis of \Cref{teo4} holds.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the normality assertion by a direct verification that A_j + A_j^T < 0 for the given bidiagonal/tridiagonal matrices.
issues.overall_effect: The stated justification for the applicability of teo4 to the synthetic example is wrong; no formal result is invalidated because dissipativity of A_1, A_2 holds anyway.
issues.title: Synthetic example: A_1 and A_2 are falsely claimed to be normal matrices
issues.why_classification: A local correction of a false justification in the experimental section; the hypothesis it was invoked to support holds by direct computation, so no claim or guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we project the Lyapunov equation~\eqref{eqn:lyap:residual} onto a smaller subspace and then use standard solvers for the small equation, thus obtaining the coordinates of the approximation in the subspace
we apply truncation when computing the approximate \GLE solution $\tilde{\fX}$, i.e., we discard all singular values smaller than the prescribed accuracy threshold $\tol$

issues.failure_explanation: The Loewner ordering P >= P~, Q >= Q~ is provable for the exact stationary iterates (a monotone Lyapunov-series argument), but the computed P~, Q~ are produced by Algorithm 2 with approximately solved inner Lyapunov equations (subspace projection) and additional truncation of small singular values; neither Galerkin approximation nor singular-value truncation is order-preserving in general. The cited theorem therefore cannot establish the asserted ordering for the computed quantities, and no other argument is given; the claim is only certified to hold up to the error tol.

failure_location.quote: As expected, the green curve lies above the blue one since $\fcP \succeq \tilde\fcP$ and $\fcQ \succeq \tilde\fcQ$. This property follows directly from an application of \cite[Thm.~3.3.16]{HorJ91}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the ordering for the exact iterates and note that for the computed Gramians it holds only up to the certified error tol, or present the plot observation as empirical.
issues.overall_effect: The explanation of the singular-value decay plot (fig2:a) rests on an unestablished ordering of the computed Gramians; no formal result depends on it.
issues.title: Unsupported claim that the computed Gramians are PSD-ordered below the exact Gramians
issues.why_classification: A local caveat suffices; the affected claim only explains a figure and can fail by at most the certified tolerance, so no substantive claim or guarantee is lost.
